question: Compare the top 3 open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products.
short_answer: Qdrant, Weaviate, and Milvus are the leading open-source vector databases. For a fast-moving RAG startup, Qdrant is recommended due to its single-binary operational simplicity and native payload filtering, while Milvus suits large-scale distributed enterprise deployments and Weaviate provides rich hybrid-search capabilities.

key_findings.claim: Qdrant is distributed as a single standalone binary and can run without external dependencies.
key_findings.supporting_quote: Qdrant is distributed as a single binary and can run without any external dependencies.

key_findings.claim: Milvus separates compute and storage components to provide cloud-native distributed horizontal scaling.
key_findings.supporting_quote: Milvus architecture separates compute and storage into decoupled layers ensuring high availability and horizontal scaling.

key_findings.claim: Weaviate integrates vector indexing with native inverted keyword indexes for out-of-the-box hybrid search.
key_findings.supporting_quote: Weaviate combines vector search with traditional keyword search algorithms to deliver out-of-the-box hybrid search capabilities.

sources.title: Weaviate Architecture and Hybrid Search Documentation

assumptions: 'Top 3' evaluated by GitHub stars, developer adoption, and cloud-native production support.
Target workload assumes low-maintenance retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
limitations: Hardware benchmark claims reflect vendor documentation rather than uniform independent evaluations.
Managed cloud pricing tiers were excluded from this self-hosted evaluation.
next_steps: Run benchmark ingest tests with startup's exact embedding dimensionality (e.g. 1536 or 3072).
